description: We’re NeuralMesh, a team of five students from Bangladesh using NASA data and technology to support farmers. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we’re building Krishi Mama to help farmers explore crop-rotation options using historical climate data and local agricultural information. We welcome teammates interested in agriculture, Earth science, data analysis, and design.
summary: Krishi Mama is a Bangla-first agricultural decision-support platform that helps Bangladeshi farmers make informed crop rotation and sowing decisions using NASA Earth observation and climate data. Farmers can explore crop options using local crop calendars, water availability, and farming priorities, while the platform turns complex observations into understandable climate insights, crop-water needs, and planting-time comparisons. An AI assistant helps explain available information and results. Initially focused on Cumilla and Chattogram, Krishi Mama connects NASA data with local agricultural knowledge to support farmer judgment.
details:
THE CHALLENGE

Krishi Mama addresses “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data.” Farmers need to consider climate, water availability, crop timing, and local conditions when planning crop rotations. These decisions become harder when useful information is scattered or presented in technical language.

WHAT WE BUILT

We built a Bangla-first decision-support web application for Cumilla and Chattogram, Bangladesh. It connects NASA environmental observations with Bangladesh crop-calendar information through a public crop-rotation comparison tool, climate-data pages, and a personal farm workspace.

HOW IT WORKS

Farmers provide their district, current crop sequence, soil and water information, and farming priorities. The tool compares the existing sequence with two alternatives, showing crop-water requirements, broad calendar overlaps, and historical temperature conditions that need local review.

The current crop choices include Aman rice, Boro rice, Aus rice, and mustard. A separate crop-transition feature explores historical conditions between selected harvest and sowing periods.

NASA DATA

NASA POWER supplies historical temperature, rainfall, humidity, and solar-radiation context. GPM IMERG provides dated precipitation observations. SMAP provides regional surface soil-moisture observations, and MODIS provides vegetation-greenness indices.

NASA POWER climate information is used in the rotation screening. Satellite observations provide additional environmental context; they are not direct measurements of an individual farm.

DATA QUALITY

Observations that fail the application's quality checks are withheld. Missing values are not treated as zero. Incomplete GPM records are not presented as complete daily rainfall totals. Observation dates help distinguish historical samples from current conditions.

FARMER EXPERIENCE

Visitors can explore climate information and compare crop sequences without signing in. Account features support a personal farm workspace. Bangla and English interfaces, simple explanations, and expandable details make information easier to understand.

The AI assistant helps explain available information and results. It does not independently select a crop, change a plan, or replace farmer judgment.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

The application uses Next.js and React for the frontend, a Node.js backend, and Google Gemini for the AI-assisted explanation feature. Open-Meteo supplies short-term weather forecasts separately from NASA historical observations.

LIMITATIONS AND FUTURE WORK

This is a two-district prototype. Soil information is collected, but stronger soil-specific evaluation remains future work. The application does not predict yields, income, or measured soil-health improvements. Future development includes farmer usability testing, better soil-specific comparisons, and expansion to additional districts.

AI USE

Google Gemini is used to help explain user questions and available crop and environmental context. OpenAI Codex was used during development for coding assistance, debugging, interface revisions, and translation support. Team members directed the development and reviewed the application.
